podcast.title: Performance at SARS-Stock (2003)
podcast.body: The Sam Roberts Band performed at SARS-Stock on July 30, 2003, an event aimed at boosting Toronto's morale and economy after the SARS virus crisis. "Here's a bit from the Sam Robertsburg. Sar's stock on July 30, 2003."

podcast.title: Benefiting from Major Label Distribution
podcast.body: Sam Roberts is mentioned as an example of an indie musician who gained fame thanks to the distribution power of Universal, through a mutually beneficial deal with an independent label, Maple Music. This arrangement allows indie artists to achieve wider exposure. "This is an independent label with a solid roster of Indie musicians who are now famous thanks to the distribution power of Universal."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Catalyst for Band Connection
podcast.body: Max Kermann was wearing a Sam Roberts Band T-shirt on the second day of university, which prompted Nick Dica to introduce himself, saying, "I like Sam Roberts." This interaction led to Nick joining Arkells as the bassist. "And then the next day Nick introduced himself to me because I was wearing a Sam Roberts band T-shirt. And Nick said, I like Sam Roberts."

xref.title: Band Formation at McMaster University (2004)
xref.body: The band's core began forming on the first and second days Max Kermann attended McMaster University in Hamilton in 2004. Max, who was primarily interested in finding bandmates, met Mike DeAngeles on day one by asking about his favorite bands (The Weakerthans) and if he played guitar. On day two, Nick Dica introduced himself to Max because Max was wearing a Sam Roberts Band T-shirt, and upon learning Nick played bass, he was also invited to join. "You're literally the first and second day that you were in university."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Band Recruiting Strategy at McMaster
xref.body: On his first day at McMaster University, Max Kermann proactively sought out potential band members. He met Mike DeAngeles by asking about his favorite bands and instruments. On the second day, Nick Dica approached him because of his Sam Roberts Band T-shirt, and Max quickly recruited him for bass. "I did immediately start profiling people on campus and seeing, this is like the kind of person that would want to be in a band with me. And on the first day I met Mike and on the second day I met Nick."

xref.title: Hamilton Local Act and Influence
xref.body: The Constantine's were a band that frequently played in Hamilton venues like the Casbah and Underground around 2006, during what was considered the "Golden Age" of indie rock. Their guitar-driven indie rock sound influenced Arkells' early musical direction, particularly on songs like "The Boss Is Coming." "So every week at the club it seemed like at the Casbore, the Underground there was bands like Winner Sleep or Joel Plasket, Constantine, Stars, Sam Roberts, Arcade for all of these bands just coming through Hamilton that we got to go."
